method: Each flow in namespace w11 was published by POST /api/v1/main/flows (YAML), run by POST /api/v1/main/executions/w11/<id>, polled until terminal, then 3 s later its logs were read with GET /api/v1/main/logs/<executionId> (no filters) and the execution with GET /api/v1/main/executions/<id>. The artifact was brought up with `docker compose -p w3oracle up -d` and taken down with `down -v`.
how_to_read_for_egret: `findings[].egret_expected` is what W11 Task 3 asserts. A `basis` of `egret-chosen` marks a deliberate difference from the measured Kestra behaviour, stated in the spec. `raw_records` is evidence, not an egret expectation.

level_table_notes.log_task: a Log task with `level:` stores at that level; `log_task_default` is the level with none declared
level_table_notes.cap_summary: egret-only: Kestra has no per-attempt cap
level_table_notes.values: every value is a member of `level_set`

findings.finding: A script task's stdout line is logged at INFO, on both runners.

A stderr line is logged at ERROR, not WARN, on both runners, and `warningOnStdErr` does not change the level: default, `false` and `true` all logged ERROR. The property exists on shell plugin 1.9.8 (each flow deployed 200) and in all three runs the task ended SUCCESS, so on this artifact it did not change the state either. This matches the Java (`PluginUtilsService.parseOut`: `else if (isStdErr) runContext.logger().error(line)`) and contradicts egret's `ingest_line`, which returns `Level::Warn`. egret keeps not offering `warningOnStdErr`; that is a schema fact, not a log expectation, so it is not asserted here.

A whole-line `::{"outputs":{...}}::` is NOT logged, on stdout and on stderr, and its values reach the task's outputs: a downstream Log rendered `k=v k2=v2`. Only a line that IS a marker counts: a line that merely contains one (`x ::{...}::`) or has a trailing space is logged verbatim at INFO and not consumed. The execution API returns `outputs: null` on every task run on this artifact, so the value was read through a downstream Log, not off the execution. egret's comment in `ingest_line` ("consumed as an output AND logged") is wrong about Kestra.

invalid_marker_warning.note: one WARN per invalid whole-line marker; between prefix and suffix is serde_json's error text, not Jackson's. Kestra's shape (WARN + DEBUG stack) is measured; the text and the absent stack line are chosen

findings.finding: `##kestra:log:debug##` switches later stdout lines to DEBUG until `##kestra:log:info##`; neither marker line is logged. It applies on the Docker runner too. A stderr line inside the bracket stays ERROR (stderr is tested before debug in `parseOut`). The mode lives in one `DefaultLogConsumer` shared by both streams, and the Java tests the marker before the stream, so a marker on either stream toggles it (the stderr-marker case is from the Java, not measured). DEBUG lines are stored with the task's default log level: `logLevel: TRACE` changed nothing, and TRACE lines are stored too.

sequence.note: `stored` is in input order; Kestra reads the two streams on two threads, so its order across streams varies

findings.finding: The execution log holds no worker framing line. The worker's `Type {} started` / `Type {} with state {} completed in {}` (`WorkerTaskProcessor`) and the executor's `Flow completed with state {}` go through `Logs.logTaskRun`/`logExecution` to the server's slf4j logger, not the execution log. 0 of 127 lines across 17 executions have a null `taskId` (an execution-level line would). A Log-only flow stores exactly one line (with framing it would be 3). Log with a list `message` stores one line per element. Fail stores ERROR `<errorMessage>` and then a DEBUG Java stack trace.

Script tasks add their own lines around the output: DEBUG `Starting command with pid N [<cmd>]` (or `with container id ...`), DEBUG `Command succeed with exit code 0`, TRACE `Captured 0 output file(s).`, and on Docker TRACE `Container created/deleted` and `Volume created/deleted`. A failed attempt adds ERROR `io.kestra...TaskException: Command failed with exit code 1`, a DEBUG stack trace and ERROR `Command failed with exit code 1`. These are the runner's and the worker's, not the task output.

egret_expected.note: Kestra's exceptionHandler logs every throwing task's message at ERROR unless killed; RunContextLogger then adds an ERROR line of the cause-chain messages when there is a cause, and a DEBUG stack trace. q4 (Fail: ERROR + DEBUG, no cause) and q5 (script: ERROR `io.kestra...TaskException: Command failed with exit code 1`, DEBUG, ERROR cause `Command failed with exit code 1`) show both shapes. egret has no cause chain and writes only the first line: `cause_line_count` and `stack_trace_line_count` 0 are stated divergences. The text matches Kestra for Fail and timeout; for other handlers `{failure_message}` is egret's own. `future_dropped` follows Kestra's KILLED (no line). No pid/container/volume diagnostics

findings.finding: `attemptNumber` is 0-based: the failing first attempt's lines carry 0 and the retry's carry 1, with the same `taskRunId`. It equals the index into `taskRun.attempts` (2 attempts: FAILED then SUCCESS). `{{ taskrun.attemptsCount }}` rendered 0 then 1. egret's `TaskInput.attempt` is 1-based (`jsonb_array_length(attempts)`, claim.rs).

findings.finding: Kestra does NOT store a 100,000-char line whole, and does not cut it either: it SPLITS it into 15,360-char pieces (`RunContextLogger.MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 1024 * 15`, `Splitter.fixedLength`), each a separate INFO line with the same timestamp. 6 x 15,360 + 7,840 = 100,000, nothing lost. Because the pieces share a timestamp, the API returned them out of order: the 7,840-char remainder came back at position 5 of 7 (Process) and 3 of 7 (Docker), not last. There is no volume cap. The input was ASCII only, so whether Kestra counts UTF-16 code units (Java `String.length()`, which `Splitter.fixedLength` uses) or code points was not observable here; the Java counts UTF-16 code units.

egret_expected.note: user decision D6: split as Kestra splits. The piece length and the equal timestamps are measured. Two chosen differences: egret counts Unicode scalar values (Rust `char`), Kestra's Java counts UTF-16 code units, so they differ only for text outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, where Java can also split a surrogate pair (unmeasured); and egret returns the pieces in input order (ascending id), where the artifact returned them out of order
